lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Barbara, this is Ana. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about fruit at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good. Busy, but good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 5 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than I thought. 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stick to two beers if I eat first. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I just didn't feel like it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You just weren't feeling it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the vegetables fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, getting started makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel so much better on Sunday when I don't overdo it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My kids is why I'm doing this. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the vegetables. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You kept going even on a hard week. That says a lot about you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the late dinners keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Being around for my family is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I keep it to 3 drinks on the weekend.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the late dinners gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the late dinners made this week harder, you still got 5 days in, and your plan is to keep it to 3 drinks on the weekend. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Barbara. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Strong change talk about limiting drinks and family
Shifted away from energy change talk
Moved past strong change talk at line 40

flags.reason: Repeats the same water-between-drinks advice from line 18 without new permission or response to participant's 'Maybe'.
Participant said they can keep to two beers and don't want to end up like their dad; coach moved to advice instead of reflecting or exploring.
Participant said they want their energy back; coach switched to a closed question about daughter instead of reflecting.
Participant said they didn't think they'd like it but do and want to keep up with grandkids; coach moved on without reflecting.
Participant's fruit-at-night question was raised at line 4 and never addressed.

score.summary: Coach closed well with a clear goal, a backup plan, and a concise summary, and offered autonomy throughout. However, several strong change statements (lines 23, 28, 40) were moved past or met with advice, and the water tip was repeated without new permission.
strengths: Line 39 and line 55 reflect the participant's family motivation and ambivalence with real meaning.
Line 62 summarizes the week and the agreed goal, and line 60 builds a barrier plan in the participant's own words.
Line 15 and line 38 emphasize that the plan belongs to the participant.
coaching_tips: Reflect change talk at line 23 ('I can stick to two beers if I eat first') before offering any advice.
Do not repeat the line 18 advice at line 26; ask permission or wait for the participant to invite it.
At line 28 and line 40, reflect the energy and grandkids motivation ('You want your energy back') before asking a new question.
Address the fruit-at-night question raised at line 4 or confirm it can wait.
